docs/onchain-analytics/raw/defillama-dex.note: TASK-007 task 007-2 — the vendor's own DEX-volume chain list, live-recorded keyless. src/adapters/defillama/dex-chains.ts is GENERATED from it, so this file decides which chains the engine advertises dex.volume.history on. The generator test compares the committed module against a regeneration from this evidence — editing BOTH would pass that check, which is precisely the gap this pin closes.

packages/core/test/fixtures/defillama/de.note: TASK-007 task 007-4 — live-recorded vendor response (trimmed to 120 daily points, protocols[] dropped). The gapless-92-point acceptance test rests on it; a silent edit would be indistinguishable from the vendor changing its answer.

TASK-007 task 007-4 — live-recorded HTTP 200 zero-volume shape (narrower key set, change_1d null). It is the EVIDENCE that a missing aggregate must normalize to null rather than 0; hand-editing it would turn a measured vendor behaviour into an assumption.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/defillama-dex.note: TASK-007 backlog item 6 — live keyless verification that DeFiLlama's `chain` echo equals the `vendors.defillama` name we send, for all 274 covered chains. It is the evidence that normalizeDexVolume's identity guard cannot misfire on a covered chain, and (incidentally) the first measured proof that a COVERED chain can return `total24h: null` — the justification for nullable aggregates, which until now cited a chain that is not covered.

packages/core/test/fixtures/defillama/de.note: TASK-007 / WI-17 (D-2) — live-recorded response for the includeSeries:false mode (excludeTotalDataChart=true), 2026-07-28. It answers a question that was previously a guess: the vendor KEEPS `totalDataChart` and sets it to an empty array rather than omitting it or sending null. That is what decides window/points/gapDays in that mode, so a silent edit here would rewrite a measured vendor behaviour into an assumption.
